title: Purity conjugation of coefficient-adjunction diagrams and cocycles
statement:
Let $I$ be a preordered set and for every $i\in I$ let $\mathcal X_i,\mathcal Y_i$ be categories [def-nagata-category], functors $P_i:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal Y_i$, $J_i,H_i:\mathcal Y_i\to\mathcal X_i$, a specified adjunction $P_i\dashv J_i$ with unit $\eta_i^J$ and counit $\epsilon_i^J$, and a natural isomorphism $\gamma_i:H_i\xrightarrow{\sim}J_i$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For $i\le j$ let $C^X_{ji}:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X_j$, $C^Y_{ji}:\mathcal Y_i\to\mathcal Y_j$ be functors, and supply natural isomorphisms $b_{ji}:C^Y_{ji}P_i\to P_jC^X_{ji}$ and $c_{ji}:C^X_{ji}J_i\to J_jC^Y_{ji}$. Suppose, with composition right to left, that for every $M\in\mathcal X_i$, $K\in\mathcal Y_i$,
$$J_j(b_{ji,M})c_{ji,P_iM}C^X_{ji}(\eta_i^J(M))=\eta_j^J(C^X_{ji}M),$$
$$\epsilon_j^J(C^Y_{ji}K)P_j(c_{ji,K})b_{ji,J_iK}=C^Y_{ji}(\epsilon_i^J(K)).$$
Then the formulas
$$\eta_i^H(M)=\gamma_{i,P_iM}^{-1}\eta_i^J(M),\qquad \epsilon_i^H(K)=\epsilon_i^J(K)P_i(\gamma_{i,K})$$
are the unit and counit of an adjunction $P_i\dashv H_i$, and
$$a_{ji,K}=\gamma_{j,C^Y_{ji}K}^{-1}c_{ji,K}C^X_{ji}(\gamma_{i,K})$$
is a natural isomorphism $C^X_{ji}H_i\to H_jC^Y_{ji}$. It satisfies both typed identities
$$H_j(b_{ji,M})a_{ji,P_iM}C^X_{ji}(\eta_i^H(M))=\eta_j^H(C^X_{ji}M),$$
$$\epsilon_j^H(C^Y_{ji}K)P_j(a_{ji,K})b_{ji,H_iK}=C^Y_{ji}(\epsilon_i^H(K)).$$

For $i\le j\le k$ suppose natural associators $\alpha^W_{kji}:C^W_{kj}C^W_{ji}\xrightarrow{\sim}C^W_{ki}$, $W=X,Y$, are specified, and that
$$J_k(\alpha^Y_{kji,K})c_{kj,C^Y_{ji}K}C^X_{kj}(c_{ji,K})=c_{ki,K}\alpha^X_{kji,J_iK}.$$
Then the conjugated comparisons satisfy exactly
$$H_k(\alpha^Y_{kji,K})a_{kj,C^Y_{ji}K}C^X_{kj}(a_{ji,K})=a_{ki,K}\alpha^X_{kji,H_iK}.$$
The same $b$ cocycle remains valid because $b$ is unchanged. If identity-extension comparisons $b_{ii},c_{ii}$ are identities under specified coefficient unitors, then so is $a_{ii}$. No compatibility between the different $\gamma_i$ is assumed: the middle $C^X_{kj}(\gamma_j)$ and $C^X_{kj}(\gamma_j^{-1})$ factors cancel. The conclusions require neither faithfulness of the $C$ functors nor any conservativity of a reduction functor.

proof.text: For each i construct adjH_i := (adjJ_i).ofNatIsoRight (gamma_i).symm using Mathlib CategoryTheory.Adjunction.ofNatIsoRight. Its defining unit is eta^J followed by gamma_i inverse, and its counit is P_i(gamma_i) followed by epsilon^J. The Mathlib unit and counit formulas give exactly the first two asserted equalities. This uses the existing adjunction transport construction directly instead of reconstructing its natural Hom bijection.

proof.text:
Fix $i\le j$ and abbreviate $U=C^X_{ji}$, $V=C^Y_{ji}$, $b=b_{ji}$, $c=c_{ji}$. Set $a_K=\gamma_{j,VK}^{-1}c_KU(\gamma_{i,K})$. Its inverse is $U(\gamma_{i,K}^{-1})c_K^{-1}\gamma_{j,VK}$. For $t:K\to K'$, the three naturality equations give
$$H_j(Vt)a_K=\gamma_{j,VK'}^{-1}J_j(Vt)c_KU(\gamma_{i,K})=\gamma_{j,VK'}^{-1}c_{K'}U(J_i(t)\gamma_{i,K})=a_{K'}U(H_i(t)).$$
The two inverse composites cancel adjacent inverse factors. Hence $a$ is a natural isomorphism.

proof.text:
With the abbreviations of Step 2, substitute the formulas of Steps 1 and 2 in the unit expression and cancel $U(\gamma_{i,P_iM})U(\gamma_{i,P_iM}^{-1})$. Naturality of $\gamma_j^{-1}$ at $b_M:VP_iM\to P_jUM$ gives
$$H_j(b_M)a_{P_iM}U(\eta_i^H(M))=\gamma_{j,P_jUM}^{-1}J_j(b_M)c_{P_iM}U(\eta_i^J(M))=\gamma_{j,P_jUM}^{-1}\eta_j^J(UM)=\eta_j^H(UM).$$
The middle equality is exactly the assumed $J$-unit identity.

proof.text:
For the counit expression, substitution cancels $P_j(\gamma_{j,VK})P_j(\gamma_{j,VK}^{-1})$. Naturality of $b$ at $\gamma_{i,K}:H_iK\to J_iK$ then gives
$$\epsilon_j^H(VK)P_j(a_K)b_{H_iK}=\epsilon_j^J(VK)P_j(c_K)P_jU(\gamma_{i,K})b_{H_iK}=\epsilon_j^J(VK)P_j(c_K)b_{J_iK}VP_i(\gamma_{i,K})=V(\epsilon_i^J(K))VP_i(\gamma_{i,K})=V(\epsilon_i^H(K)).$$
The penultimate equality is the assumed $J$-counit identity, applied at $K$.

proof.text:
For $i\le j\le k$, substitute both $a$ formulas in the left side of the claimed cocycle. Naturality of $\gamma_k^{-1}$ at $\alpha^Y_K$, followed by cancellation of $C^X_{kj}(\gamma_{j,C^Y_{ji}K})$ with its inverse, leaves
$$\gamma_{k,C^Y_{ki}K}^{-1}J_k(\alpha^Y_K)c_{kj,C^Y_{ji}K}C^X_{kj}(c_{ji,K})C^X_{kj}C^X_{ji}(\gamma_{i,K}).$$
The assumed $c$ cocycle changes this to
$$\gamma_{k,C^Y_{ki}K}^{-1}c_{ki,K}\alpha^X_{J_iK}C^X_{kj}C^X_{ji}(\gamma_{i,K})=\gamma_{k,C^Y_{ki}K}^{-1}c_{ki,K}C^X_{ki}(\gamma_{i,K})\alpha^X_{H_iK}=a_{ki,K}\alpha^X_{H_iK},$$
where the equality is naturality of $\alpha^X$ at $\gamma_{i,K}$. This is precisely the required cocycle, with the specified associators.

proof.text:
For the identity clause, write the specified unitors as $u^W:C^W_{ii}\xrightarrow{\sim}1$. Being the identity under these unitors means $c_{ii,K}=J_i(u^Y_K)^{-1}u^X_{J_iK}$. Naturality of $\gamma_i$ at $u^Y_K$ and of $u^X$ at $\gamma_{i,K}$ gives
$$a_{ii,K}=H_i(u^Y_K)^{-1}\gamma_{i,K}^{-1}u^X_{J_iK}C^X_{ii}(\gamma_{i,K})=H_i(u^Y_K)^{-1}u^X_{H_iK}.$$
Thus $a_{ii}$ is the identity under the same unitors. The $b$ comparisons, associators and unitors were unchanged, so any originally specified $b$ cocycle or identity equation remains literally the same equation. All cancellations used actual natural isomorphisms; no faithfulness, conservativity or relation between different $\gamma_i$ was used.
